title: Five automated quality checks against raw Online Retail
prescribes: Audit a table on five axes -- completeness, uniqueness, freshness, referential integrity and value validity -- with thresholds agreed in advance so results are pass/fail, not vibes.
applied: Ran all five bundled checkers against the 541,909-row raw retail extract, using a 48-hour freshness SLA and business rules (quantity >= 1, price > 0, known country list).
narrative: 5 of 5 checks fail, and every failure is real. 25% of order lines carry no CustomerID, which silently removes a quarter of revenue from any customer-level analysis -- the reason phase 3's cohort work states its population explicitly.

The freshness check fails by design: the newest invoice is from 2011, so against a 48-hour SLA the lag is enormous. On a historical Kaggle extract that is expected; wired to a live warehouse table the same check is the one that pages someone.

Referential integrity is the interesting one: 61.49% of 2011 order lines belong to customers with no 2010 history. Against a static dimension table that reads as an orphan; in reality it is new-customer acquisition, which is exactly why this check needs a human verdict.
Value validation catches the cancellations -- negative quantities encoded as C-prefixed invoices -- and the long tail of countries outside the top-ten list.

takeaway: A quarter of retail order lines are anonymous, so every customer-level number in this lab is computed on an explicitly stated subpopulation rather than on 'the data'.
